sections.overview: Nomada leucophthalma is an early-spring cuckoo bee associated with the mining bees Andrena clarkella and A. apicata.
sections.identification: The sexes are similar; a British account describes a black, brown and yellow bee, while reliable separation from other Nomada requires diagnostic characters.
sections.habitat: It is found with its hosts in open woodland, heath and moor; these are also landscapes where the host bees forage on willows in early spring.
sections.diet: Adults visit flowers for nectar, but females lack pollen-collecting equipment; the larva takes food stored by its host.
sections.behavior: The British account gives a flight period from March to mid-May and reports adults near host burrows; N. succincta uses other Andrena hosts and flies later into summer.
sections.reproduction: The female enters nests of A. clarkella or A. apicata; their early activity and willow-pollen specialization help explain the parasite’s spring schedule.
sections.ecology: A classic chemical-ecology study found the same major scent compound in A. clarkella and male N. leucophthalma, consistent with chemical resemblance in this host-parasite pair.
sections.conservation: BWARS does not consider the species scarce or threatened in Britain; this is a regional statement, not a global assessment.
